rows.title: Hammerspoon SIGTRAPs sending an hs CLI result to a client that already gave up
rows.note: All three crashes (10-02 14:25:15, 10-03 11:26:51, 10-08 08:44:06) fault in ipc_callback -> ipc_sendMessage -> CFMessagePortSendRequest -> CFMessagePortIsValid (freed port, PAC check): hs.ipc's COMMAND handler sends RETURN to a client whose port died while the command ran or waited. 10-02 and 10-03 each have an hs CLI crash 0-4 s earlier whose parent had already exited; 10-08 has none (a SIGKILL leaves no report) and test_llm_limits_grok, which killed its hs after 3 s, ran in the minute before. Hammerspoon answers one client at a time, so a test client queued behind another suite's harness (instruction gate ~11 s) outlived its -t (default 4 s) or its python kill bound. Fix: every live hs call in llm-legs and hammerspoon tests waits under /usr/bin/lockf -k -t 600 /tmp/hs-cli.lock with hs -t >= 20 and a kill bound past both; tests/test_hs_cli_lock.sh in both repos keeps it; the retry loops of test_presence and test_dia_js (for concurrent suite clients) are gone. Not fixed, same chain still open: production callers run hs unlocked with the default 4 s -t (llm-legs bin/claude-chat-switch, claude-resume-timer, llm-selfcheck, llm-reset-redeem; hammerspoon bin/claude-keys, claude-latency; claude-setup hooks/compact-auto.sh, session-trash.sh; the BTT TypeWhisper.toggle action) and can still queue behind a test harness; a Lua guard in init.lua was not tried, as it cannot be tested without crashing the live Hammerspoon. Ruled out for these crashes: AX polling and leaked drawings (neither in the faulting stack). Side finding: hammerspoon tests/test_menu_cache.sh is red on the night base (test_menu_cache.lua:141, Reports title.text nil), unrelated.

rows.title: com.egor.harness-doctor exits 1 while the Speed collector it execs ends in KeyError on a Lost time class with no lever
rows.note: The 7 exit-1 runs (harvest 10-09 18:26..10-10 00:26) are bin/speed-doctor, which harness-doctor's exec_speed replaces itself with, so its exit is the job's: ~/Library/Logs/harness-doctor.log ends in 7 'Speed: error · KeyError: 'refusal'' lines (log mtime 22:42), a 5-min job between share/time_budget.py gaining the refusal class and 9d76b38b (22:47) adding its TIME_LEVERS entry; the next harvest (16 runs) has none. Fix here: tests/test_speed_doctor.sh pins every time_budget.FLOORS class and gate refusal row to a TIME_LEVERS lever (red with the refusal lever removed). Ruled out: harness-doctor's own collect (guarded_collect turns its exceptions into an error document; the log's older TypeError tracebacks predate the window, their line numbers match a <3,000-line file vs 6,268 now); exit 1 on a Speed error stays, the menu shows it too.

blind_spots.what: which short-lived or other users' process writes the internal SSD
blind_spots.reason: Each tick reads the disk counters of our own live processes (proc_pid_rusage), but a process that dies between ticks takes its counters along, and other users' counters need root; the 2026-10-04 privileged sample put ~76% of writes on our own short-lived processes
blind_spots.would_catch_if: a consented privileged sample (fs_usage or per-process rusage of every uid)

blind_spots.what: the parents of processes that live less than the 2 s window outside storms
blind_spots.reason: Births are attributed from the newborns still alive at the window's end; a storm (2,000 births/s for 2 min or kernel share 0.5) adds a 60 s census polling every 20 ms, at most every 30 min, so calm hours still lean toward longer-lived children
blind_spots.would_catch_if: an exec event stream (endpoint security, root)

blind_spots.what: idle wakeups, disk bytes and footprints of Apple and third-party items
blind_spots.reason: proc_pid_rusage of other users' processes needs root, so their cohort score counts CPU, births and launches only and lists W, D, R and M as unknown

blind_spots.what: which hs CLI client was inside Hammerspoon when it crashed
blind_spots.reason: A Hammerspoon ipc crash report names no client; an hs killed by a timeout leaves no report of its own, so the client is inferred from the suites running in the tick before
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the hs calls journaled their start, end, exit and caller
